Source: http://www.toddmccormick.org

Posted September 11, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: Todd is a close friend, but his case is one of the most outrageous excesses of the war on the sick, dying and disabled.)
See
Cancer Victim Todd McCormick In Solitary Confinement. Medical Neglect Leaves Him in Pain.

Written on September 2, 2000 entered as email by Todd’s mother, Ann McCormick.

Since Raid: 1129 days
In Prison: Day 243
In the hole: Night 19

Dear Friends and Fellow Activists,

It's been all too long since I have had access to email. A lot has happened since I surrendered to the court on January 3, 2000 at 2:30pm. Aside from spending the past 243 days in the federal prison system and being witness to the darkest side of the War on Drugs (users and their families), I've had to mourn the loss of a dear friend, Peter McWilliams (6/14/00),
See
The Murder of Peter McWilliams -- An Indictment, Not an Obituary – by Richard Cowan
and worry madly about a man who has been like a father to me for many years, Jack Herer, who had a stroke July 14, 2000.
See
Tommy Chong To Emcee Jack Herer Benefit.

The lesson is always the same, life is a very delicate gift, not to be taken for granted or to be lived meekly - by taking the easiest route or tossing aside one's principles for the sake of some fleeting perception of security. 'Security' is never attained. It will remain elusive to us all our lives. At age 8, I reached the conclusion that there was no security in life.

Coming to prison has been somewhat enlightening. What our government calls a Federal Correctional Institution does no correcting at all. The guards/CO (correctional officer) know about as much about 'correcting' as President Clinton knows about inhaling.

I've also come to realize that this is their ultimate punishment. This is what they hold over our heads to insure that we stay in line. It's a joke!

I surely miss family and friends... my dogs. Watching the sunset over the open ocean... and all the things that are beautiful and sacred in life. But, I am sure if more people were exposed to the reality that is 'prison', more people would stand up to protect even the most basic, fundamental rights.

Why do I feel they would be more willing to take a stand after experiencing first hand the repercussions. They would realize that they lose far more by not demanding that this kind of oppression end.

A friend of ours, Bobby, once came up with the idea of a National Turn-Yourself-In Day. Imagine every smoker, grower, farmer, medical patient - who cannot plant so much as a non-narcotic HEMP seed – walking into police stations around the country simultaneously and demanding, " Arrest me and give me a trial NOW - or leave me alone forever. " Prohibition would pop like an over-inflated balloon. But, that will never happen because everyone is afraid of being where I am right now.

Think of the patients who are so afraid that they won't even try cannabis --It might work and that would make it hard to keep believing the age old ideologies. They would rather go blind from glaucoma than to accept that their government has been lying to them.

I say that we should not fear. I'm in the heart of the monster and feel no fear. I'm writing this from a maximum security cell (AKA: the 'Hole') in a medium/high security federal prison in Los Angeles at Terminal Island.

Why am I in the hole?
A urine sample detected traces of cannibinoids. This is the first and only time I have been drug tested since I came in. They had no baseline comparison.

When the results came back I instantly became the most punishable medical marijuana patient in the state of California. The punchline to this not so funny joke is that the C.O. who handcuffed me told me that he had voted for 215 in 1996.. and he wished me well. I chuckled over the irony.

Last month, the warden wished me luck after reading about the Oakland club and that the 9th circuit court of appeals injected some logic into the proceedings forcing Breyer to lift his injunction.

But, even the warden seems afraid to do anything more than extend his condolences ...

Q: How many people will comply with a system and toss out their principles for something they feel will provide 'security'?
A: TOO MANY!!!!

For the past decade, my activism has been about applying freedom in every area of my own life. To some my actions appeared bold; that I was daring the government to change or challenge.

I honestly say, that in a million years, I never would've expected we would get to the time for the trial and be denied the right to tell the truth in the courtroom. Truths like my 30 years of medical records/history. Truths like Prop 215, the government's own compassionate use program, expert testimony from doctors. We were ordered not to even utter the word 'medical' before 'marijuana' to a jury of my peers!
See
Buckley Denounces Prosecution of McCormick and McWilliams In Strongest Terms Yet.
" On the eve of the trial Judge King decided, so to speak, to eliminate the Bill of Rights. "

Was I surprised? YES!
Shocked? COMPLETELY!!!
Outraged? ABSOLUTELY!!

This brings us to a topic that many people have had questions about. Why did I take a deal? Why didn't we go through with a trial?

Right up to the 11th hour, I was holding firm that I wanted to go to trial anyway, even 'defenseless'. At that time I still believed that even if I lost at trial, I could stay free on bond while awaiting the appeal. Then they dropped another bombshell.

My lawyers and I were told that appeal bond is not allowed for defendants convicted of a crime that carries a 10 yr to Life sentence. I, again, felt shock and disbelief. The only way to stay out on bond was to plead guilty to a charge carrying a lesser sentence. It seemed the only way to stay out on appeal bond while I continued to fight my case.
See
McCormick and McWilliams Plead Guilty to Avoid Ten Year Minimums.
McCormick Reserves Right To Medical Necessity Defense.
Sentencing Set for February 28.

To go through a trial, unable to speak the truth, barred from defending ourselves, a trial was looking like a very expensive 'go directly to jail' card. I chose to put my faith in the appeal court, which, in retrospect, now knowing the 9th District's position on medical necessity, was the best decision.

I had hoped to remain free. --as free as one is under pre-trial release.. (call into an officer of the court twice a week, go to the federal building twice a month (1st & 15) call an 800 # every night between 7-11pm to listen for my number to come up so I could go pee in a cup for them the next day..)

If you can even call that free! Had I known for even a moment that I would have been locked up anyway, I would have gone through the trial.

As in my childhood, dealing with a recurrent cancer, I'm looking at this as having potential to be a positive experience - which, while it is happening is hard to appreciate. Years from now I hope that there is something from this I was glad to have experienced.

I would like to say thank you to all the people who have been sending inspiration and support via snail mail.

MAIL CALL IS THE HIGHLIGHT OF THE DAY! It's the only high point, actually. I've been a bit slow returning letters lately, but I will get to everyone.

Everyone has been asking what I can receive. The answer is, Not much. Paperback books, photos - not instant, magazines (except those that talk about growing cannabis ..not that I would know anything about that subject anyway..)

Also, several people have asked if I need money (on my books). Sarah, the wonderful woman who produces the SPITFIRE events - that I have been fortunate to have been touring with - held a Benefit last May at the House of Blues in LA.. Some of my friends, Bill Maher, Krist Novoselic, Perry Farrell, Michael Franti and Spearhead, Andy Dick, Exene Cervenka came down, at their own expense to help raise funds to both support me while I'm in here and to help with the case. I mention them because I want to thank them dearly for their support.
(MarijuanaNews note: Marc Emery contributed $1000 that night.)
See
MarijuanaNews To Attend 'Spitfire' Concert In LA To Raise Money For Imprisoned Medical Marijuana Patient, Todd McCormick, At House of Blues Sunday, May 7th.

Also, Kennedy and Larry Flynt, both of whom had wanted to take part, but one was having a baby and the other was at a funeral.

I want to give special praise to Bill Maher. He has not hesitated to bring attention to both my situation and this great hypocrisy called the WAR On DRUGS. He is as great an activist as any I have ever known - and an even greater friend.

I implore everyone to pick up a copy of the September issue of GEAR magazine. Turn to page 136 and read Bill's latest [biased opinion] titled 'Tokin' Justice'

An excerpt:
" ..tens of thousands of people doing jail time for pot when they shouldn't be - that is not inconsequential.. Todd says anyone would quickly understand the pernicious nature of the Drug War if they could spend just a day with the other prisoners: most in for something having to do with drugs - yes, some truly nefarious, but most, not. You'd be surprised, he says, how civilized it is inside Terminal Island. Why? Because a lot of who is there are you and me. You know, nice people.. "

"..I hear them say " Zero Tolerance " a lot these days. I guess it's a matter of what you have 'zero tolerance' for. I have it for injustice, and I invite you to share my indignation with anyone who will listen that MY friend, could be YOUR friend, and he doesn't belong behind bars. "

The long version is much better.

I don't know if that article is already on the web, but if it is not, could someone pick it up, type it in and send it around? And please mail me a few copies to share with a few non-computer using friends. I don't have access to a photo copy machine now that I am in the 'hole'.

I'm sure they can't hold me hostage forever. I look forward to my release when I can once again be typing my own emails.

Peace, Love and Happiness,

Todd Patrick McCormick
P. O. W. #11071-112
P.O. Box 3007
Terminal Island, CA 90731
(MarijuanaNews note: I strongly urge everyone to write Todd, or at least to send him a card. Something humorous would be appreciated, I am sure.)
